newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to raise withholding tax on bond earnings.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to raise withholding tax on bond earnings.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Friday the government planned to scrap a scheme to charge income tax on interest earnings from government bonds and Treasury bills, and instead will increase the withholding tax from the current 10 percent.

"We have complaints from our citizens that they are ready to to pay more withholding tax instead of the tedious task of filling out tax forms to declare their interest income," he told reporters before a cabinet meeting.

"We are considering their demand to save our citizens from this drudgery. We can postpone this decree if it is necessary. The citizens say they are ready to pay an additional tax when they receive cash payments from their interest income at maturity," he said.

Turkey imposed the 10 percent withholding tax on the interest income from treasury bills and bonds to be issued from November 1 with 1997 maturity, as part of the government's revenue raising packages.
An income tax exemption on government bond and treasury bill yields will expire on December 31. The government is now expected to extend the exemption.
Erbakan also denied rumours that the government would replace the national currency, the lira, with another one, but said Turkey would take measures to make it stronger in 1997.
